en.title: Respect for elders
en.summary: How older people are addressed and cared for, and the language of polite offers.

paragraphs: Respect for older people is shown by manners and by actions. This lesson teaches titles, polite offers and the vocabulary of age.

In English-speaking countries, older people are usually called Mr, Mrs or Ms with their surname unless they ask you to use their first name. Younger people give up their seat on a bus and hold a door open. A teenager meets her grandfather on a bus in Norwich.

lines.speaker: Grandad
lines.text: Thank you, dear. That is very kind.

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: Would you like me to carry your bag?

lines.speaker: Grandad
lines.text: No, I can manage. But I appreciate it.

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: How is Grandma? Is she feeling better?

lines.speaker: Grandad
lines.text: Much better, thank you. She'd love to see you on Sunday.

lines.speaker: Girl
lines.text: I'll come after lunch. Shall I bring anything?

paragraphs: **1. Polite titles.** Use Mr, Mrs or Ms with a surname for adults you do not know well. Ms is neutral about marital status. See Introduction to Grammar: Substantives (nouns).

blocks.html:
TitleUsed forExample
Mra manMr Brown
Mrsa married womanMrs Clark
Msany womanMs Davies
Dra doctor or PhDDr Patel

paragraphs: **2. Would you like me to...? offers help.** It uses an object pronoun and the infinitive. See Introduction to Grammar: Pronouns.

blocks.html:
FormExample
Would you like me to + verb?Would you like me to carry it?
Shall I + verb?Shall I open the door?
Can I help you with...?Can I help you with your bag?
Let me + verbLet me hold the door.

items: Elderly is polite; old can sound blunt. Many people say older people or senior citizens.
Grandad and Grandma are informal; Grandfather and Grandmother are formal.
A care home looks after people who cannot live alone.
I appreciate it means I am grateful for it.

paragraphs: Many older people in Britain live independently or in care homes, and families keep in touch by visiting and by telephone. Respect is shown more by manners and visits than by living together.
